# Conformance

<!-- Generated by `npm run conformance`. Do not edit by hand. -->

biolint is scored against test corpora maintained by other projects. They are not vendored: `node scripts/corpora.ts` fetches them at pinned commits.

- **hts-specs**: https://github.com/samtools/hts-specs at `510c107ba89a`
- **vcf-validator**: https://github.com/EBIvariation/vcf-validator at `19125af2b120`
- **BioFmtSpecimens**: https://github.com/BioJulia/BioFmtSpecimens at `a88ddc9ceca0`
- **biopython**: https://github.com/biopython/biopython at `86e9ea56dbd6`
- **fasta_validator**: https://github.com/linsalrob/fasta_validator at `a7cbc40f4264`
- **genometools**: https://github.com/genometools/genometools at `5cd9b0fe1e78`
- **acidbio**: https://github.com/hoffmangroup/acidbio at `f3a01593060a`

Each corpus file is labelled valid or invalid by its authors. biolint is run in the strict profile, and a file counts as rejected when at least one error is reported.

The two VCF corpora overlap heavily (the hts-specs files were derived from vcf-validator), so they are not independent evidence.
The two FASTQ suites are not independent: the BioFmtSpecimens FASTQ files are copies of the Biopython test files. They differ only in where the labels come from (file names in Biopython, an index file in BioFmtSpecimens).
FASTA has no formal specification, and every BioFmtSpecimens FASTA file is labelled valid, so that suite can only show false rejections; the files meant to be rejected come from the small fasta_validator suite.
GFF3: the BioFmtSpecimens labels are read from its `GFF3/index.yml`. GenomeTools files have no labels of their own: a file counts as valid or invalid when the GenomeTools test suite (`testsuite/gt_gff3_include.rb`, `gt_gff3validator_include.rb`) runs `gt gff3` or `gt gff3validator` on that file alone, without options, and expects exit status 0 or 1. Files that the suite only runs with options, or pipes through other commands, are not scored. Exit status 0 includes files that GenomeTools accepts while printing a warning the suite checks for (a blank after the seqid, a negative `##sequence-region` coordinate).
GFF3: agreement is counted per file, not per reason. Four GenomeTools files (`cds_check_fail_1` to `_4`) are rejected by both, but for different reasons: GenomeTools objects to a CDS phase that does not follow from the preceding segments, which biolint does not check, and biolint objects to an empty source column in the same files.
GTF: no third-party collection of GTF files labelled valid/invalid was found. The only labelled material is six files in the GenomeTools test data, and their labels are the exit status its test suite (`testsuite/gt_gtf_to_gff3_include.rb`) expects from the converter `gt gtf_to_gff3` run without options. A converter fails for reasons of its own as well as for format errors, so this suite is weak evidence.
GTF: one of the five agreements on invalid files is a coincidence. `gt_gtf_to_gff3_test_inconsistent_strand2.gtf` is rejected by GenomeTools because a transcript is on the other strand than its gene; biolint compares strands within a transcript only, and rejects the file in strict mode because `transcript_id` is not the second attribute and a start codon has no frame.
The acidbio files are labelled for one BED type each (the directory name), which is information the files themselves do not carry. biolint infers the layout from the first data line, so a file whose only defect is on that line in its last standard column is read as having a custom column there; those cases are listed as deliberate disagreements.

## Disagreements

Every one of the 304 disagreements is classified:

| Verdict | Files | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| corpus-error | 68 | the label contradicts the specification, or the file has a second, unintended defect |
| corpus-outdated | 10 | the label follows an earlier revision of the specification |
| beyond-spec | 129 | the corpus enforces a convention of its own validator that the specification does not state |
| deliberate | 37 | biolint knowingly differs |
| not-implemented | 60 | a real requirement that biolint does not check yet |
| open | 0 | not yet explained |

| Verdict | Corpus label | Files | Reason | Example |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| corpus-error | valid | 12 | Line 7 has an empty source column. The specification requires `.` for an undefined field; GenomeTools happens to accept an empty one. | `genometools/testdata/cds_check_succ_1.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 11 | A record with no ALT allele carries three GL values. Number=G is one value per genotype, and one allele has one diploid genotype. (In 4.4/4.5 the same file also has the malformed float `-0r.58`.) | `4.1/passed/passed_body_alt.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 8 | The file contains END=0 on a record at POS 100 (END cannot precede POS) and, from 4.3, an SB value with one number where the reserved definition is Number=4. | `4.1/passed/passed_body_info.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 8 | An INFO line is declared `Number=A,Type=Flag`. Every version requires Number=0 for a Flag. | `4.1/passed/passed_meta_info.vcf` |
| corpus-error | invalid | 7 | The file is separated by single tabs throughout, and §1.7 allows whitespace in the name in exactly that case; §3.2 only recommends against it. biolint warns (BED030). | `BED04/bad/04-name_with_spaces.bed` |
| corpus-error | valid | 3 | A meta line has a value starting with `<` that is not a list of key=value entries; from 4.3 such a line is structured and needs an ID. | `v4.3/passed/complexfile_passed_000.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 3 | The FORMAT key `G%3AS` does not match the key syntax `[A-Za-z_][0-9A-Za-z_.]*` required from 4.3. | `v4.3/passed/passed_body_format.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 3 | Two ##contig lines share an ID, which VCF 4.3 and later forbid explicitly. | `v4.3/passed/passed_meta_contig.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 2 | A genotype is written `0/0\|`, with a trailing phasing separator, which the GT grammar does not allow. | `v4.4/passed/passed_body_sample_format_CICN.vcf` |
| corpus-error | valid | 2 | The `##sequence-region` has a negative coordinate. GenomeTools only warns unless run with -strict (the same test suite expects -strict to fail); GFF3 coordinates are positive integers. | `genometools/testdata/sequence_region_negative_end.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | Records of one contig are split by another contig, which VCF 4.3 forbids ("must form a contiguous block"). | `4.3/passed/complexfile_passed_000.vcf` |
| corpus-error | invalid | 1 | The file (`@HD VN:1.6 GO:none`) is byte-for-byte identical to passed/hdr.HD6.sam in the same corpus, and `none` is a valid GO value. | `sam/failed/hdr.HD3.sam` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | The line `@PG ID:fork-1b PP:fork-1b` names itself as its previous program; the specification says PP must match another @PG line (samtools warns about it too). | `sam/passed/hdr.PG4.sam` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | A blank line splits the sequence of the second record. NCBI states that blank lines are not allowed in the middle of FASTA input and samtools faidx cannot index the file; the index entry itself notes that BioPerl, where the file comes from, considers it invalid. | `BioFmtSpecimens/FASTA/badfasta.fasta` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | `##gff-version 3` is on line 3, after two comment lines written by gffread; the specification requires it to be the topmost line. (The default profile accepts the file.) | `BioFmtSpecimens/GFF3/ERCC92.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | Each gene and its transcript share one ID (the transcript line reads `ID=X;Parent=X`), so the IDs are not unique, which the specification requires. | `BioFmtSpecimens/GFF3/mm9_sample_ensembl.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | The file holds only FASTA records and has no `##gff-version` line, which the specification says must be present. (The default profile accepts the file with a warning.) | `BioFmtSpecimens/GFF3/only_fasta.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | The seqid ends with a space. GenomeTools removes it with a warning; the specification says a seqid may not contain unescaped whitespace. | `genometools/testdata/gt_gff3_whitespace_problem.gff3` |
| corpus-error | valid | 1 | The file tests that all reserved tag names are accepted and fills them with the placeholder `xxx`; `Gap=xxx` is not a Gap string as the specification defines it. | `genometools/testdata/uppercase_attributes.gff3` |
| corpus-outdated | invalid | 8 | The contig name uses `*` away from the first position, which the 2019 revision of the VCF 4.3 naming rules made legal. | `4.3/failed/failed_body_chrom_004.vcf` |
| corpus-outdated | invalid | 1 | Colons in contig names were made legal by the 2019 revision of VCF 4.3; the sibling corpus has a passing file with one. | `4.3/failed/failed_body_chrom_001.vcf` |
| corpus-outdated | valid | 1 | Chromosome names such as `NM_007524.1` contain a dot. The specimen was labelled against the UCSC description, which has no naming rule; BED v1.0 §1.5 restricts chrom to letters, digits and underscore. biolint accepts the file in its default profile. | `BioFmtSpecimens/BED/vgLoadMahoney-clonePcr.bed` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 36 | ##SAMPLE, ##PEDIGREE and ##META are described only by example. biolint checks their syntax and that IDs are unique, not their vocabulary. | `4.1/failed/failed_meta_sample_000.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 28 | No version requires a field order inside structured meta lines; VCF 4.4 states that implementations must not rely on it. | `4.1/failed/failed_meta_alt_004.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 24 | The specification permits several records at one position. biolint reports exact duplicates as a warning (VCF501) and does not normalise alleles to find equivalent representations. | `4.1/failed/failed_body_duplicated_000.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 16 | ##ALT lines have no Number or Type field in any version; extra fields are free-form. | `4.1/failed/failed_meta_alt_001.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 16 | The specification does not define what makes a ##assembly or ##pedigreeDB URL valid. biolint only requires that it is not empty. | `4.1/failed/failed_meta_assembly_001.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 3 | The seqid breaks the `md5:<checksum>:<name>` convention, which is a GenomeTools extension and not part of GFF3. | `genometools/testdata/md5_seqid_missing_seqid.gff3` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 2 | VCF 4.1 and 4.2 place no restriction on colons in contig names. | `4.1/failed/failed_body_chrom_001.vcf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 1 | A `##sequence-region` line comes after a feature on that sequence. GenomeTools requires the directive first; the specification does not say where it must be. | `genometools/testdata/gt_gff3_test_27.gff3` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 1 | A stop_codon line lies five kilobases beyond the last exon of its transcript. The converter needs a CDS next to the stop codon to merge the two; GTF 2.2 has no such rule, and biolint does not check that codons lie inside exons. | `genometools/testdata/gt_gtf_to_gff3_test_fail_no_flank.gtf` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 1 | A thirteenth column after twelve valid BED fields is a custom field (BED12+1, §1.3 and §1.10). The corpus rejects it only because the directory expects exactly BED12, which the file itself cannot declare. | `BED12/bad/12-bed13.bed` |
| beyond-spec | invalid | 1 | The line is a consistent BED12 feature followed by 22 further columns, which the specification allows as custom fields (BED12+22). The index gives no reason for the label, and the twelve standard fields break no rule. | `BioFmtSpecimens/BED/overlapSelect-wideIn.bed` |
| deliberate | invalid | 20 | The only defect is on the first data line, the line biolint infers the layout from. Nothing in a BED file says which columns are standard (§4), so the column with the bad value and those after it are read as custom fields, with a note (BED013) quoting the value; the same value on any later line is an error. | `BED07/bad/07-string_thickStart.bed` |
| deliberate | valid | 4 | Records of one contig are split by another contig. 4.1/4.2 say such blocks "should" be contiguous; biolint treats it as an error in strict mode because indexing fails either way. | `4.1/passed/complexfile_passed_000.vcf` |
| deliberate | valid | 4 | Two ##contig lines share an ID. Uniqueness is stated only from 4.3, but parsers of every version keep a single definition, so biolint reports it throughout. | `4.1/passed/passed_meta_contig.vcf` |
| deliberate | valid | 2 | The corpus tests the syntax of optional fields only (its README defers SAMtags semantics) and names tags after their type (`BC:B:`, `H1:H:`, `H2:H:`); biolint also holds BC, H1 and H2 to the types SAMtags predefines for them (Z, i, i). | `sam/passed/aux.pass-B.sam` |
| deliberate | valid | 2 | One line carries `Ontology_term` twice. The specification writes several values as one comma-separated list and does not say what a repeated tag means; GenomeTools rejects it and biolint follows in strict mode (a warning by default). | `BioFmtSpecimens/GFF3/knownGene.gff3` |
| deliberate | valid | 1 | The file is empty (0 bytes). biolint reports an empty file as an error for every format (TXT010) because it nearly always means a failed step, and `samtools view` refuses it as well. | `BioFmtSpecimens/SAM/xx#blank.sam` |
| deliberate | valid | 1 | Sequence lines contain pairs of spaces (the "cutpoints" of a BioRuby test) and three records reuse an earlier identifier. Spaces are not residue codes in the NCBI description and shift the coordinates of a faidx index, so biolint reports them as errors; some parsers strip them. | `BioFmtSpecimens/FASTA/example1.txt` |
| deliberate | valid | 1 | The file has `#` comment lines before, between and after the records, a Biopython test of its own leniency (the file says "I don't really know if FASTA format is supposed to support this"). No description of FASTA has `#` comments, and samtools faidx stops at the first one. | `BioFmtSpecimens/FASTA/f003.fasta` |
| deliberate | valid | 1 | Ten of the fourteen records reuse an earlier identifier (`seq3`, `seq4`, ...). Parsers read the file, but an index keeps only the first record of that name (samtools faidx: "Ignoring duplicate sequence"), so biolint makes duplicate identifiers a warning by default and an error in the strict profile. | `BioFmtSpecimens/FASTA/pictogram.fasta` |
| deliberate | valid | 1 | A parser stress test: one ID is used on chr9 and chr30, and features on chr17 name a chr9 feature as Parent. The specification does not forbid either in so many words; biolint follows GenomeTools, which rejects both. | `BioFmtSpecimens/GFF3/knownGene_out_of_order.gff3` |
| not-implemented | invalid | 40 | Semantic rules for structural variants introduced in VCF 4.4 (SVCLAIM, tandem-repeat keys, CN/CICN, phase-set lists) are not checked yet. | `v4.4/failed/failed_CNV_001.vcf` |
| not-implemented | invalid | 16 | Semantic rules introduced in VCF 4.5 (local alleles, base modifications, computed END, FORMAT LEN) are not checked yet. | `v4.5/failed/failed_body_invalid_format_LAA_1.vcf` |
| not-implemented | invalid | 4 | chromEnd is 4294967296 on chr20, beyond the end of that chromosome (§1.6). Checking it needs chromosome sizes, which biolint does not take; without them the specification allows values up to 2^64−1, so biolint only warns (BED024). | `BED03/bad/03-chromEnd_too_large.bed` |

These classifications are the judgement of the biolint authors, not of the corpus maintainers. The full list is in `conformance/results.json`.
